reasoning: As of March 6, 2026, Delcy Rodríguez was sworn in as acting president on January 5, 2026, with a 90-day mandate from Venezuela's Supreme Tribunal of Justice. The 90-day period would end around April 5, 2026, just before the April 30 resolution date. Key uncertainties: (1) Whether she maintains power beyond the 90-day mandate; (2) Whether opposition forces (Machado/González) successfully challenge her; (3) Whether the Trump administration continues supporting her; (4) Constitutional requirements for new elections. She has shown some compliance with U.S. demands (releasing prisoners), earning temporary Trump support. However, the opposition remains uninstalled and the political situation is highly volatile. The narrow window between mandate expiration (April 5) and resolution date (April 30) creates significant uncertainty about succession arrangements.
